summary: SQLite WAL checkpointing is the process of transferring committed transactions from the write-ahead log (WAL) file back into the main database file. This operation is critical for preventing the WAL from growing unbounded and for maintaining read performance, as readers must search the WAL file linearly. By default, SQLite performs automatic PASSIVE checkpoints when the WAL reaches 1,000 pages. For more aggressive cleanup, developers can manually trigger FULL (blocks until completion), RESTART (resets the WAL index), or TRUNCATE (physically shrinks the file) checkpoints. However, long-lived read transactions can cause "checkpoint starvation," leading to WAL bloat. A significant concurrency bug in the checkpointer, which could lead to data loss, was resolved in SQLite version 3.53.0 (March 2026).

claims.text: Checkpointing transfers committed transactions from the WAL file back into the original database file.
By default, SQLite triggers an automatic checkpoint when the WAL file reaches a threshold of 1,000 pages.
Automatic checkpoints are exclusively performed in PASSIVE mode.
PASSIVE checkpointing is non-blocking and may not run to completion if concurrent readers or writers are active.
FULL checkpoint mode blocks until all concurrent readers and writers have finished (or a timeout occurs) to ensure all WAL pages are copied to the database.
RESTART checkpoint mode behaves like FULL but also resets the WAL index to frame 1, allowing subsequent writes to overwrite the WAL file from the beginning.
TRUNCATE checkpoint mode behaves like RESTART but additionally truncates the WAL file on disk to zero bytes.
Read performance deteriorates as the WAL file grows because readers must check the WAL for the most recent version of a page, and the time to check is proportional to the WAL size.
Long-lived read transactions can cause 'checkpoint starvation' where the checkpointer cannot advance past the oldest active read transaction, leading to unbounded WAL growth.
A concurrency bug in the checkpointer known as the 'WAL-Reset bug' could cause data loss and database corruption; this was resolved in SQLite version 3.53.0 (March 2026).
